subject: Repeated request stalls and p99 tail — Atlas Retail escalation
messages:
From: Ravi Srinivasan <ravi@atlasretail.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas SRE <sre@atlasretail.com>
Date: 2028-05-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Repeated stalls on product search (p99 spike) — urgent

Team,

We're seeing repeated stalls on product search and cart recs starting late last night (2028-05-04 ~22:00 UTC). P95 looks stable but p99 is spiking to 8–12s and some requests are timing out. Impact: delayed checkout flows and a handful of abandoned carts.

I've attached a short excerpt from our request logs and a couple trace ids (trace: at-0452f3, at-0452fa). Can your team confirm whether this is on your side or a traffic pattern change? We attempted to reroute to a fallback model but see the same tail.

Can you please prioritise — this is high-impact for our holiday promo.

Thanks,
Ravi
Head of Platform
Atlas Retail

Attachments: atlas_request_log_excerpt.txt

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Srinivasan <ravi@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-05T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Repeated stalls on product search (p99 spike) — urgent

Thanks Ravi — we see the alerts and I’m on it. I’ve looped in Dev (runtime), Lauren (SRE) and Marissa (AM). Initial read shows elevated queue depth for Atlas routed requests on our shared inference pool; we’re pulling traces now.

Short plan:
- Dev to triage traces and queue metrics (now)
- If concurrency cap is hit, temporary bump + route Atlas traffic to a warm dedicated pool (if available)
- I’ll keep you updated every 60 mins and follow up with mitigation ETA

Sofia
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-05T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Repeated stalls on product search (p99 spike) — triage notes

Quick findings from the first 45m of data:

- Telemetry: sustained concurrency cap hits on shared pool S-P1 between 2028-05-04T22:05:00Z and 2028-05-05T02:40:00Z for Atlas routing prefix. Token ingestion rate did not drop — requests queued instead.
- Queueing/backpressure pattern: average queue depth jumped x6, queue latency contributed ~70% of the p99. No sign of immediate downstream model OOMs.
- KV cache: higher than normal cold-miss on prefix keys for the Atlas workload (likely new prefix distribution from the holiday promo), increasing per-request model time.
- Error rate: small increase in 504s when requests timed out at the front-end gateway, correlating with queue saturation.

Attachments: p99_traces.zip (selected traces showing queued time)

Recommended short-term mitigations (to stop the customer impact):
1) Increase Atlas per-customer concurrency cap on S-P1 from 120 -> 240 for 2 hours (manual override) — reduces queueing immediately.
2) Enable aggressive prefix pre-warm/cache policy for Atlas route for 6 hours.
3) If caps still hit, failover Atlas traffic to DedicatedPool-D2 (warm) — warmup script should be run first (estimated 18 mins).

I'll attach the slice of traces to the ticket (INF-2371). If we get go-ahead, I can implement (1)+(2) immediately.

— Dev
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Srinivasan <ravi@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-05T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Repeated stalls on product search (p99 spike) — mitigation proposal

Ravi — thanks for raising this. We recommend the following immediate steps which we can execute as soon as you confirm:

1) Temporary concurrency bump to 240 for Atlas on the shared pool for 2 hours
2) Aggressive prefix caching for Atlas traffic (6 hours)
3) If you prefer, we can fail traffic to a dedicated pool (DedicatedPool-D2) — note: will take ~18 minutes to rotate and warm KV cache.
4) As a gesture for customer impact, Redwood will offer a 10% service credit for the affected window once we validate the impact window.

Please reply with which option you prefer (bump + cache vs dedicated failover). If we don't hear in 30 mins we'll start with (1)+(2) to reduce user impact.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, North America
Redwood Inference
